hypothesis: If domestic dogs descend from several wild species, dog genomes will fall into multiple lineages each more closely related to a different wild canid species, rather than forming a single clade with one wild species.
pass_criterion: In a whole-genome phylogeny and admixture analysis using NCBI canid genomes, dog breeds fall into at least two separate lineages, each nested within a different wild canid species (wolf, jackal, coyote), with bootstrap of 90 or more.
fail_criterion: All dog genomes form one monophyletic clade nested within grey wolf (Canis lupus) lineages, with bootstrap of 90 or more, and no breed groups with a non-wolf species.
interpretation: 'Descended from several wild species' means multiple independent domestication origins from different species. The modern test is whether dog nuclear genomes are monophyletic relative to wolves, coyotes and jackals. Later gene flow between dogs and wolves is not counted as separate descent.

dataset.name: NCBI Datasets Genome: Canis lupus familiaris (taxon 9615)
dataset.why_it_fits: The page lists dog genome assemblies with downloadable FASTA and annotations. Wolf, coyote and jackal assemblies are available from the same portal for comparison.
